analysis:
The only changes in this batch are in docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump, a note that Gemma 4 is exempt from tensor-parallel-first placement, the new 'Gemma 4 tensor-parallel foundation' section (head lines 4038-4240), and a rename of the SwitchLinear source path. No executable code, configuration or security controls change, so a regression cannot come from this diff itself.

The new text describes security-relevant behavior that the next pass should check against the code. It was not verifiable from the docs alone:
- The Gemma TP resident runtime uses a keyed, authenticated data plane with a sealed all-sum (line 4093). The load agreement binds fingerprint, plan, prompt policy, selection, lanes, KV storage and prefix cache (4106-4111), and mismatched peers refuse before weights are read.
- Load verifies the whole artifact and each tensor's shape before reading, with a host memory gate (4100-4105). This fits the existing TB-007 and TB-002 assumptions.
- Gemma TP prompt prefixes use the memory tier and the owner's encrypted SSD tier, restored only after a sealed vote and confirmation (4145-4152). This falls under T-041. The docs say behavior follows the Gemma pipeline's prefix cache. They do not state whether the cacheSalt/tenant partition scope is applied the way GLM's `prefixScope` is (visible only in the line-4248 text for GLM). The next pass should confirm Gemma TP prefix keys and HMAC lookup tags fold in the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, and that `DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_PREFIX_CACHE=off` is honored. The docs say prefix cache is on by default for Gemma TP.
- The fastest-plan rule (4193-4231) changes placement policy only. It does not affect trust.
- Stated gaps: memory-tier prefixes are not charged, there is no measured activation floor, and media and speculative decoding are not built. These are documented limitations, not regressions.

No finding is raised because only documentation changed and no concrete security defect is evidenced. The Gemma TP source (Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix, runtime) was not supplied, so the prefix-scoping claim is an unverified contract.
